**Cyclique is a desktop application for organisers of recreational cycling groups in Singapore.** Manage cyclist profiles and group rides through typed commands, with cyclist cards and a separate Rides panel showing your data at a glance.
![Cyclique showing cyclist profiles and the Rides panel](docs/images/release-v1.4/cyclists-and-rides.png)
* Store cyclists' contact and emergency numbers, Functional Threshold Power (FTP), experience levels and preferred cycling locations.
* Find cyclists by supported profile fields and view matching cyclist cards alphabetically.
* Create, edit, find and delete group rides with dates, locations, distances, minimum power and maximum group sizes.
* Add eligible cyclists to a ride, remove them from its roster and display its registered cyclists. Duplicate membership, capacity and minimum-power checks help you manage registrations.
* Keep cyclist and ride data between sessions through automatic saving to a local JSON file.

You will need Java 25. Follow the [Quick start](https://ay2627s1-cs2103t-w11-1.github.io/tp/UserGuide.html#quick-start) instructions to download and launch the app. The [User Guide](https://ay2627s1-cs2103t-w11-1.github.io/tp/UserGuide.html) explains the commands and their validation rules.
Cyclique is based on [AddressBook-Level3](https://se-education.org/addressbook-level3/), created by the [SE-EDU initiative](https://se-education.org/).
We are a team based in the [School of Computing, National University of Singapore](https://www.comp.nus.edu.sg).
You can reach us at the email `seer[at]comp.nus.edu.sg`

title: Ride feature bug testing report
Review ride creation, editing, deletion, roster addition/removal, roster listing, ride finding,
field validation, live filters and JSON loading. Run the entire automated suite, including existing
cyclist commands, emergency contacts, deletion confirmation and storage tests.
to select equivalence partitions and adjacent boundary values. This is a targeted audit, not an
exhaustive proof of correctness or a completed cross-platform manual test campaign.
Existing staged defensive-programming changes remain in place; this audit does not stage,
commit or push changes. Production fixes are confined to JSON loading/validation and argument tokenisation.
Five reproduction tests failed before the production fixes; all pass afterwards. A sixth control
case, a valid roster exactly at capacity, passed before and after.
| Defect | Impact and reproduction | Fix and regression |

| JSON null root escapes normal error handling | Put `null` in the saved book. `JsonUtil.readJsonFile` calls `Optional.of(null)`, throwing an uncaught `NullPointerException`. It bypasses the application's normal loading recovery. | Reject a deserialised null root inside the existing I/O error path so it becomes `DataLoadingException`. `RideDataIntegrityTest.read_nullJsonRoot_reportsLoadingFailure` covers the actual file boundary. |

| Duplicate roster members load | Save the same phone twice in a ride roster. It loads successfully, inflates occupancy and can trigger the roster-removal membership assertion when assertions are enabled. | Reject duplicate phones during ride conversion with a checked validation error. `RideDataIntegrityTest.read_duplicateRosterMember_reportsLoadingFailure`. |

| Over-capacity rosters load | Save two members on a ride with maximum group size 1. Loading accepts a state that CLI additions prohibit. | Compare saved roster size with the validated group size before constructing the ride. `RideDataIntegrityTest.read_overCapacityRoster_reportsLoadingFailure`. |

| Missing cyclist references load | Save a roster phone absent from the cyclist list. The book loads, but `ridelist` cannot display that roster and reports a missing-member error. | Validate all roster references against the complete cyclist list before exposing the loaded book. `RideDataIntegrityTest.read_missingCyclistReference_reportsLoadingFailure`. |

| Tabs can silently swallow an edit field | Run `rideedit 1 notes/Bring lights<TAB>s/2`, with a literal tab. The old tokenizer treats `s/2` as part of notes, leaving maximum group size unchanged while reporting success. | Recognise whitespace before prefixes, advance searches explicitly and ignore empty prefixes. Preserve embedded prefix-like text within values. `RideRosterIntegrationTest.execute_tabSeparatedRideEdit_updatesBothFields` checks both fields and persistence; `ArgumentTokenizerTest` covers separator classes. |
Loading rejects the whole invalid book through the existing recovery mechanism rather than dropping
members silently. The startup behaviour after a loading failure remains an empty book. Back up a
corrupted file before using that recovery session to save new data. Direct storage reads in the
regression tests verify that rejection itself leaves the original file unchanged.
Three pre-existing round-trip test fixtures contained roster phones with no cyclist records.
Update those fixtures to reference an existing cyclist or add the corresponding test cyclists;
retain their original assertions about ride details, notes, IDs and persistence.
The table separates inputs expected to be accepted from those expected to be rejected.
Validity depends on the operation: empty notes are valid when clearing an edit but invalid when
supplied during creation. A valid find query may return no matches; that is not invalid input.
| Area | Valid partitions and boundary values (accepted) | Invalid partitions and boundary values (rejected) | Evidence |

| Country code and subscriber length | Country-code lengths 1, 2 and 3; subscriber lengths 3 and 4. Examples: `+1 123`, `+12 123`, `+123 123`, `+123 1234`. | Country-code lengths 0 and 4; subscriber length 2. Examples: `+ 123`, `+1234 123`, `+123 12`. | `PhoneTest`, `EditCommandParserTest` |

| Distance | Positive numbers within the precision and digit limits: 0.01/0.02 and 999999.98/999999.99. | Non-numeric, negative, zero, excessive precision and excessive whole digits: `NaN`, `1e2`, -0.01, 0, 0.001 and 1000000. | `RideBoundaryIntegrationTest`, existing `DistanceTest` |

| Minimum power | Whole numbers within 1–600: 1/2/599/600. | Below/above the range, fractions and integer overflow: 0/601, 1.5 and 2147483648. | `RideBoundaryIntegrationTest`, existing minimum-power tests |

| Maximum group size | Positive whole numbers up to nine digits: 1/2/999999998/999999999. | Zero, more than nine digits and fractions: 0/1000000000 and 1.5. | `RideBoundaryIntegrationTest`, existing `GroupSizeTest` |
| Notes | Missing optional notes; empty edit to clear notes; 1/9/10 words. | 11 words; blank notes explicitly supplied during creation. | `RideBoundaryIntegrationTest`, existing `NotesTest` |

| Calendar and clock | Real dates, including 29-02-2000 and 29-02-2028; valid month ends; times 0000/2359; four-digit year endpoints 0001/9999. | Non-leap-century dates 29-02-1900 and 29-02-2100; 31 April; day 32; months 00/13; times 2360/2400 and five-digit time; five-digit year 10000. | `RideDateTimeTest` |

| Ride periods | End equal to or one minute after start; edits that remain consistent with the preserved endpoint. | End one minute before start, including edits whose supplied endpoint conflicts with the preserved endpoint. | `RideBoundaryIntegrationTest` |

| Find date ranges | Ordered or equal bounds; date-only defaults of 0000/2359; `all` to reset. For valid queries, rides exactly on the bounds match; those one minute outside do not. Empty results are valid. | Inverted ranges, with `to/` earlier than `from/`. Malformed dates/times are rejected as listed above. | `RideBoundaryIntegrationTest`, existing predicate/parser tests |

| Criteria and identifiers | At least one valid criterion; positive existing ride IDs. The value 2147483647 is syntactically valid but is tested as an unknown ID at execution. | Missing criteria, required blank fields, duplicate prefixes, ID 0, negative IDs and integer overflow. Syntactically valid but unknown IDs are rejected at execution. | `RideBoundaryIntegrationTest`, existing ride parser tests |

| Roster state | Add an eligible cyclist to a roster with space; remove a joined cyclist; saved roster exactly at capacity. FTP 180/181 meets minimum 180; empty and full rosters are valid states. | Duplicate additions, removal of a cyclist who has not joined, unknown cyclist/ride, addition to a full roster and FTP 179 against minimum 180. Saved duplicate members, over-capacity rosters and missing cyclist references are rejected. | `RideBoundaryIntegrationTest`, `RideDataIntegrityTest`, existing roster integration tests |
Two further groups check state transitions rather than classifying individual values:
* **Filters and ID lifecycle:** deleting the selected roster's ride empties its cyclist display;
a later ride receives a new ID; selected roster changes update the display live; independent
ride filters are preserved. Evidence: `RideBoundaryIntegrationTest` and existing
* **Rejected-operation state:** invalid syntax and invalid command-state combinations must leave
the complete book, current cyclist list, current ride list and saved bytes unchanged. Evidence:
the shared helper in `RideBoundaryIntegrationTest`, used for 63 field-rejection combinations
Numeric valid-boundary edits are reloaded from JSON. Invalid field partitions run through creation,
editing and finding; invalid period edits correctly use command errors rather than parser errors
when validation needs the existing ride. The boundary suite complements existing unit tests instead
of assuming that parser acceptance alone proves command execution or persistence correctness.
## Deferred minor findings and policy questions
* **Ride-ID padding inconsistency:** `ridelist 01` parses as ride 1, while
`rideaddcyclist 01 +65 91234567` is rejected. Edit/delete/list use a general positive-integer
helper while roster parsing uses `[1-9][0-9]*`. Ordinary unpadded IDs work. Standardise this
accepted format in a later increment.
* **Distance error-message omission:** 999999.99 is accepted and 1000000 is rejected, but the
distance constraint message and User Guide do not explain the six whole-digit limit.
The limit is protected by tests; clarify the message/docs or deliberately change the limit later.
* **Year zero policy:** `01-01-0000 0000` is accepted by Java's proleptic calendar. The product
only specifies a real four-digit date. Decide whether the intended year range starts at 0001
before treating this as a validation defect.
* **FTP changes after joining:** lowering a cyclist's FTP below an existing ride minimum is
currently allowed. The guide describes a minimum needed to join, while ride edits protect
existing participants. Decide whether eligibility must remain true after cyclist edits;
this audit preserves the current policy rather than silently removing memberships or rejecting edits.
The ID, distance and year-zero observations were checked directly against the rebuilt classes
using JDK 25 JShell. No unrelated behaviour changes were made for these minor/policy items.

This project uses Gradle for **build automation and dependency management**. **We recommend reading [this Gradle tutorial from se-edu/guides](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/gradle.html).**
The following commands perform common Gradle tasks.
* **`clean`**: Deletes the files created during the previous build tasks (e.g. files in the `build` folder).
* **`shadowJar`**: Uses the Shadow plugin to create the fat JAR file `build/libs/cyclique.jar`.
**`runShadow`**: Builds the application as a fat JAR, then runs it.
* **`checkstyleMain`**: Runs the code style check for the main code base.
**`checkstyleTest`**: Runs the code style check for the test code base.
* `./gradlew clean test`: Cleans the project before running all tests
This project uses GitHub Actions for CI. The necessary workflow configuration files are in `.github/workflows`. No further setup is required.
As part of CI, Gradle generates JaCoCo coverage reports from the tests, and CI uploads the coverage data to Codecov. Codecov then provides information about test coverage.

However, because Codecov is known to run into intermittent problems (e.g., report upload fails) due to issues on the Codecov service side, the CI is configured to pass even if the Codecov task failed. Therefore, developers are advised to check the code coverage levels periodically and take corrective actions if the coverage level falls below desired levels.
To enable Codecov for forks of this project, follow the steps given in [this se-edu guide](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/codecov.html).

In addition to Gradle checks, CI runs repository-wide checks. Unlike Gradle checks, which cover files used in the build, these checks cover every repository file and enforce rules that are hard to apply on development machines, such as line-ending requirements.

These checks are implemented as POSIX shell scripts, and thus can only be run on POSIX-compliant operating systems such as macOS and Linux. To run all checks locally on these operating systems, execute the following in the repository root directory:
Any warnings or errors will be printed out to the console.

* Checks are implemented as executable `check-*` scripts within the `.github` directory. The `run-checks.sh` script will automatically pick up and run files named as such. That is, you can add more such files if you need and the CI will do the rest.
* Check scripts should print out errors in the format `SEVERITY:FILENAME:LINE: MESSAGE`
* SEVERITY is either ERROR or WARN.
* FILENAME is the path to the file relative to the current directory.
* LINE is the line of the file where the error occurred and MESSAGE is the message explaining the error.
* Check scripts must exit with a non-zero exit code if any errors occur.

The ***Architecture Diagram*** given above explains the high-level design of the App.
The following provides a quick overview of the main components and their interactions.

**`Main`** (consisting of classes [`Main`](https://github.com/se-edu/addressbook-level3/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/Main.java) and [`MainApp`](https://github.com/se-edu/addressbook-level3/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/MainApp.java)) is in charge of the app launch and shut down.
* At app launch, it initializes the other components in the correct sequence, and connects them up with each other.
* At shut down, it shuts down the other components and invokes cleanup methods where necessary.
The bulk of the app's work is done by the following four components:
* [**`Model`**](#model-component): Holds the data of the App in memory.
* [**`Storage`**](#storage-component): Reads data from, and writes data to, the hard disk.
[**`Commons`**](#common-classes) represents a collection of classes used by multiple other components.
**How the architecture components interact with each other**
The *Sequence Diagram* below shows a confirmed cyclist deletion. The user first enters
`delete +65 91234567`, then enters `yes` through the same command box. `LogicManager`
resolves the displayed cyclist and holds the pending request without changing or saving
data. Only confirmation consumes the request, revalidates the target, deletes the cyclist
and saves the updated address book, including any affected ride rosters. The
lifelines below represent components; their internal object calls are omitted.
Each of the four main components (also shown in the diagram above),
* defines its *API* in an `interface` with the same name as the Component.
* provides its functionality through a concrete `{Component Name}Manager` class that implements the corresponding API interface.

For example, the `Logic` component defines its API in `Logic.java` and implements it in `LogicManager.java`. Other components interact with a component through its interface rather than its concrete class, preventing them from coupling to that component's implementation, as illustrated in the following partial class diagram.
The sections below give more details of each component.
The **API** of this component is specified in [`Ui.java`](https://github.com/se-edu/addressbook-level3/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/ui/Ui.java)

The UI consists of a `MainWindow` and its parts, such as `CommandBox`, `ResultDisplay`, `PersonListPanel`, `RideListPanel`, and `StatusBarFooter`. All of these, including `MainWindow`, inherit from the abstract `UiPart` class, which captures common behavior among classes that represent visible GUI parts.

The `UI` component uses the JavaFX UI framework. The layouts of these UI parts are defined in matching `.fxml` files in `src/main/resources/view`. For example, [`MainWindow.fxml`](https://github.com/se-edu/addressbook-level3/tree/master/src/main/resources/view/MainWindow.fxml) specifies the layout of [`MainWindow`](https://github.com/se-edu/addressbook-level3/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/ui/MainWindow.java). The exception is `ArtworkScreen`, which is not a `UiPart` and has no `.fxml` file (see [Opening and closing artwork](#opening-and-closing-artwork)).
* executes user commands using the `Logic` component.
* listens for changes to `Model` data so that the UI can be updated with the modified data.
* keeps a reference to the `Logic` component, because the `UI` relies on the `Logic` to execute commands.
* depends on some classes in the `Model` component because it displays `Person` and `Ride` objects from the model.
`MainWindow` is split into two columns. The left 70% holds the `CommandBox`, the `ResultDisplay` and the cyclist panel (`PersonListPanel`). The right 30% holds the ride panel (`RideListPanel`).

Each panel is given an `ObservableList` by `MainWindow` and builds one card for every item in it: `PersonListPanel` shows a `PersonCard` for each `Person` from `Logic#getFilteredPersonList()`, and `RideListPanel` shows a `RideCard` (laid out by `RideListCard.fxml`) for each `Ride` from `Logic#getFilteredRideList()`. Because the panels observe these lists, they refresh by themselves when cyclists or rides are added, edited, deleted or filtered. `RideCard` keeps its text formatting in small static methods so that they can be unit tested without the GUI. The cards keep values such as phone numbers, distances, powers and dates on one line by replacing their spaces with no-break spaces (`DisplayText#keepTogether`), so a label can only wrap between whole values. The ride card shows the roster across its full width, because a phone number is too wide for the narrow value column. The main window has a minimum width of 720 so that the Rides panel cannot become too narrow for these values.
The two panels are filtered independently of each other:
* `find`, `list` and `ridelist ID` change only the cyclist panel. In particular, `ridelist ID` shows the cyclists registered for that ride in the cyclist panel; it does not change the ride panel.

* `ridefind` changes only the ride panel, and `ridefind all` shows every ride again. When the filter hides every ride, `RideListPanel` shows `No rides match the current filter. Use ridefind all to show all rides.` instead of `No rides yet. Use rideadd to create one.`. It tells the two cases apart using the unfiltered list from `Logic#getRideList()`.

`CommandTemplates` holds a list of `Template` records, one for each command. Each `Template` has the text shown in the Help menu and the starter text for the command box. Each menu item is a wrapping label. Whenever the **Help** menu opens, `MainWindow` builds the command items again and limits their width to the room between the **Help** menu and the right edge of the window, so a long command format wraps onto further lines instead of making the menu wider than the window. A wider window gives a wider menu, and a narrower window a narrower one. Lines wrap only between parameters, because spaces inside an optional group such as `[from/DATE [TIME]]` are replaced by no-break spaces (`CommandTemplates#keepOptionalGroupsTogether`). The menu font and padding in `DarkTheme.css` are kept small so that the height of the menu also stays inside the window. When `MainWindow` is set up, it adds one menu item per `Template` to the top of the **Help** menu, above **Full help...**. Choosing an item calls `CommandBox#setCommandText(...)` with that template's starter text. The command is only placed in the command box for the user to complete; it is not executed. The **Full help...** window (`HelpWindow`) lists the usage of every command, reusing the usage messages defined by the command classes in `Logic`, so `HelpWindow` depends on `Logic`.

`ArtworkScreen` shows a short, timed splash screen with a caption. It is drawn in code, so it is a plain class rather than a `UiPart`. `UiManager` shows the opening artwork before the main window appears, and `MainWindow` shows the closing artwork when the application exits. For this reason both classes depend on `ArtworkScreen`.
The cyclist panel observes `Logic#getFilteredPersonList()` and numbers cards from 1
using their current displayed positions. The read-only `RideListPanel` occupies the
right-hand 30% of the main window and observes `Logic#getFilteredRideList()`, so
`ridefind` changes which ride cards are displayed. It builds one `RideCard` (laid out
by `RideListCard.fxml`) for each matching ride. Ride cards show persistent IDs rather
than displayed positions. `RideCard` keeps its text formatting in small static methods
so that it can be unit tested without the GUI.

The following partial class diagram shows how the `find` and `ridefind` commands are parsed.
It omits unrelated command parsers and validation classes.
* `AddressBookParser` selects the concrete parser for the command word. For cyclist search,
`FindCommandParser` tokenises prefixes, validates each value with `ParserUtil`, creates a
`PersonMatchesFindCriteriaPredicate`, and places it in a `FindCommand`. For ride search,
`RideFindCommandParser` performs the equivalent work for ride fields and creates a
* Both concrete parsers implement `Parser`, and both use `ArgumentTokenizer`,
`ArgumentMultimap`, `Prefix` and the validation helpers shown in the diagram. A dashed
line with a hollow triangle pointing to `Parser` shows interface implementation. A dashed
arrow labelled `«create»` points to a class whose object is constructed by the class at
`ArgumentTokenizer.tokenizeWithQuotedNotes`; every other caller continues to call `tokenize`.
The existing tokenizer detects a supplied prefix after whitespace. Consequently, unquoted
`notes/Bring camera with aperture f/2` supplies both notes and minimum power; there is no way to infer intent.
The optional `notes/"Bring camera with aperture f/2"` syntax resolves that ambiguity for creation and editing.
The new entry point sorts the existing prefix positions and walks them in command order. A quote immediately
after a recognised `notes/` starts a quoted value; the first subsequent double quote closes it.
Prefix positions inside that range are excluded from argument extraction. Prefixes outside it retain their
normal meaning and ordering, including duplicates for `ArgumentMultimap#verifyNoDuplicatePrefixesFor` to reject.
During extraction, only quoted notes have their surrounding delimiters removed, before `ParserUtil#parseNotes`
and `Notes` apply word-count validation and whitespace normalisation.
Missing closing quotes, blank quoted values and non-whitespace text between the closing quote and the next
recognised prefix (or command end) throw `ParseException` with `MESSAGE_INVALID_QUOTED_NOTES`.
Both the quoted content and trailing whitespace use `Notes.isBlank`. Prefix recognition still uses
`Character.isWhitespace`: NBSP and NARROW NBSP are accepted after the quote but need an ordinary space
Backslashes are literal; embedded double quotes and escape sequences are unsupported.
Bare `notes/` still clears notes in Ride Edit, while `notes/""` is rejected rather than treated as clearing.
The tokenizer owns quote syntax; the parsers and commands retain field, ID, period and roster validation.
Parsing failure never reaches execution or saving. A malformed parameter outside valid quoted notes likewise
fails its normal validation before mutation. Other fields have no new quote semantics, and the original
`tokenize` path, including Ride Find and repeated cyclist Find criteria, is unchanged.
Quoted notes are parsed before overlap processing. Invalid quoting creates no pending ride request. If a
request is already pending, a new recognised command cancels it before parsing, even when that new input is malformed.
For example, `rideedit 1 notes/"Bring camera with aperture f/2" s/5` supplies literal notes and maximum
group size 5, leaving minimum power, ID and roster unchanged. Use an existing ride ID; normal roster constraints
still apply. `rideedit 1 notes/"camera f/2` and `rideedit 1 notes/"camera"extra f/2` are rejected without
changing or saving any ride fields. The manual regression scenario below covers these cases and explicit power edits.
`Notes` uses `Character.isWhitespace(cp) || Character.isSpaceChar(cp)` for blank detection and

The proposed undo/redo mechanism is facilitated by `VersionedAddressBook`. It extends `AddressBook` with an undo/redo history, stored internally as an `addressBookStateList` and `currentStatePointer`. Additionally, it implements the following operations:
* `VersionedAddressBook#commit()` — Saves the current address book state in its history.
* `VersionedAddressBook#undo()` — Restores the previous address book state from its history.
* `VersionedAddressBook#redo()` — Restores a previously undone address book state from its history.
These operations are exposed in the `Model` interface as `Model#commitAddressBook()`, `Model#undoAddressBook()` and `Model#redoAddressBook()` respectively.
Given below is an example usage scenario and how the undo/redo mechanism behaves at each step.

Step 1. The user launches the application for the first time. The `VersionedAddressBook` will be initialized with the initial address book state, and the `currentStatePointer` pointing to that single address book state.

Step 2. The user executes `delete 5` command to delete the 5th person in the address book. The `delete` command calls `Model#commitAddressBook()`, causing the modified state of the address book after the `delete 5` command executes to be saved in the `addressBookStateList`, and the `currentStatePointer` is shifted to the newly inserted address book state.

Step 3. The user executes `add n/David …​` to add a new person. The `add` command also calls `Model#commitAddressBook()`, causing another modified address book state to be saved into the `addressBookStateList`.

<div markdown="span" class="alert alert-info">:information_source: **Note:** If a command fails its execution, it will not call `Model#commitAddressBook()`, so the address book state will not be saved into the `addressBookStateList`.

Step 4. The user now decides that adding the person was a mistake, and decides to undo that action by executing the `undo` command. The `undo` command will call `Model#undoAddressBook()`, which will shift the `currentStatePointer` once to the left, pointing it to the previous address book state, and restores the address book to that state.

<div markdown="span" class="alert alert-info">:information_source: **Note:** If the `currentStatePointer` is at index 0, pointing to the initial AddressBook state, then there are no previous AddressBook states to restore. The `undo` command uses `Model#canUndoAddressBook()` to check if this is the case. If so, it will return an error to the user rather
than attempting to perform the undo.
The following sequence diagram shows how an undo operation goes through the `Logic` component:

<div markdown="span" class="alert alert-info">:information_source: **Note:** The lifeline for `UndoCommand` should end at the destroy marker (X), but due to a limitation of PlantUML, it continues to the end of the diagram.
Similarly, how an undo operation goes through the `Model` component is shown below:

The `redo` command does the opposite — it calls `Model#redoAddressBook()`, which shifts the `currentStatePointer` once to the right, pointing to the previously undone state, and restores the address book to that state.

<div markdown="span" class="alert alert-info">:information_source: **Note:** If the `currentStatePointer` is at index `addressBookStateList.size() - 1`, pointing to the latest address book state, then there are no undone AddressBook states to restore. The `redo` command uses `Model#canRedoAddressBook()` to check if this is the case. If so, it will return an error to the user rather than attempting to perform the redo.

Step 5. The user then decides to execute the command `list`. Commands that do not modify the address book, such as `list`, will usually not call `Model#commitAddressBook()`, `Model#undoAddressBook()` or `Model#redoAddressBook()`. Thus, the `addressBookStateList` remains unchanged.

Step 6. The user executes `clear`, which calls `Model#commitAddressBook()`. Since the `currentStatePointer` is not pointing at the end of the `addressBookStateList`, all address book states after the `currentStatePointer` will be purged. Reason: It no longer makes sense to redo the `add n/David …​` command. This is the behavior that most modern desktop applications follow.

Cyclique is designed for organisers of recreational cycling groups in Singapore who:
* have a need to manage a significant number of cyclists
* have a need to quickly access cyclists’ contact and emergency information
* organise group rides and needs to identify suitable cyclists based on factors such as preferred cycling location, FTP and experience level
* are comfortable with typing and using CLI apps

Organisers of cycling groups often have rider contact and information scattered across chats, spreadsheets, and memory, making it hard to identify suitable participants. Cyclique keeps this information in one place and helps organisers find which riders suit a given ride, based on preferred cycling location, FTP and experience level.

* Response-time requirements apply on a reference computer with a processor with at least two physical cores, 8 GB of RAM, SSD storage, and Java 25, with no other resource-intensive applications running. Record the processor model, operating system and version, and Java version with the test results.

* Measure response time from submission of a command or activation of a control until the requested information is visible and the application is ready for the next input. Exclude application startup and time spent entering input.
* Cyclique should display search or shortlist results within 2 seconds when storing up to 500 cyclists.
* Cyclique should display the cyclist list within 2 seconds when storing up to 500 cyclists.
* Adding or editing a cyclist should be completable using a single command entered from the main screen.
* Deleting a cyclist should require no more than one command and one confirmation entered from the main screen.
* Error messages should identify the invalid field, explain the violated constraint, and state the expected input format.
* Cyclist contact and emergency information must persist reliably across sessions (no data loss on app close/reopen).
* Cyclique should support storing records for at least 500 cyclists while meeting the stated performance requirements.

* Starting from the main screen with no cyclist selected or filter applied, a user who knows the target cyclist's name should be able to display that cyclist's emergency contact information within 2 user actions. Submitting one complete command (including typing it) or activating one GUI control counts as one action; each scrolling gesture also counts as one action. If names are shared, the user may use the cyclist's known phone number or email address to distinguish the target. The information should be displayed within 2 seconds of the final action under the testing conditions above.

* Cyclique should run on Windows, Linux, Unix, and macOS with Java 25 installed on computers meeting the reference hardware specification above. Only a keyboard and display should be required as input/output peripherals. Record the operating system version used for each compatibility test.
* Cyclique should store cyclist data only on the user's local computer.
* Cyclique should not transmit cyclist data to third parties.
* Data saved by the last successfully executed command should remain available after Cyclique is unexpectedly terminated and restarted.
* **Auto-save**: Automatic saving of changes to persistent storage without requiring a separate save command.
* **CLI**: *Command-Line Interface*. An interface through which the user operates Cyclique primarily by typing text commands.

* **Cyclist**: A person whose contact and cycling-related information is stored and managed in Cyclique. The terms *rider* and *member* refer to the same concept; this documentation uses *cyclist* consistently.
* **Cyclist directory**: The collection of cyclist records stored in Cyclique.
* **Cycling organiser**: The primary user of Cyclique who manages cyclist records and organises recreational group rides.

* **Duplicate cyclist**: A cyclist entry with the same phone number or email address as an existing cyclist. Email comparison ignores letter case. Identical names alone do not make cyclists duplicates.
* **Experience level**: A categorical indication of a cyclist's riding experience. Cyclique uses three experience levels: **Beginner**, **Intermediate**, and **Advanced**.

* **Functional Threshold Power (FTP)**: A cyclist's cycling performance metric, measured in watts (W), representing the highest power they can approximately sustain for an extended period. In Cyclique, FTP is recorded as a whole number from 1 to 600 W.

* **Group ride**: An organised cycling session involving one or more cyclists. The term *ride meetup* refers to the same concept; this documentation uses *group ride* unless a feature specifically uses the term *ride meetup*.
* **GUI**: *Graphical User Interface*. The visual interface through which Cyclique displays cyclist information and command results.
* **JAR file**: A Java Archive file used to package and distribute the Cyclique application.
* **Java 25**: The minimum Java platform version required to run Cyclique, based on the project constraints.
* **Local storage**: Data stored on the user's own computer rather than on a remote server.
* **Mainstream OS**: Windows, Linux, Unix, or macOS
* **Parameter prefix**: A command prefix that identifies the type of value being supplied, such as `n/` for name, `p/` for phone number, `sos/` for emergency contact number, or `f/` for FTP.
* **Persistent data**: Data that remains available after Cyclique is closed and reopened.

* **Preferred cycling location**: A location where a cyclist prefers to ride or participate in group rides. A cyclist may have more than one preferred cycling location. The special value `any`, supplied as `l/any`, indicates that the cyclist has no location restriction and is considered to match every ride location.
* **Private contact detail**: A contact detail that is not meant to be shared with others
* **Ride roster**: The list of cyclists registered or confirmed to participate in a particular group ride.
* **Validation**: The process of checking whether user input satisfies Cyclique's specified input rules before accepting it.

Cyclique is a **desktop application for organisers of recreational cycling groups in Singapore**, optimised for use through a Command Line Interface (CLI) while retaining the benefits of a Graphical User Interface (GUI). Manage cyclists, their emergency contact details and cycling profiles, and group rides by typing commands.
1. Ensure that JDK `25` is installed on your computer.
Run `java -version` in a terminal to check that the active version is `25`.
1. Copy the file to the folder you want to use as the _home folder_ for Cyclique.
1. Open a terminal, `cd` to the folder containing the JAR file, and run `java -jar cyclique.jar`.

The main window should appear after the opening artwork. When no saved data file exists, Cyclique starts with Alex Tan, Bernice Lee and Chloe Lim, and two example group rides with empty rosters, as shown below. If you already have saved data, Cyclique loads it instead.
![Cyclique main window showing three cyclists with SOS numbers and two group rides](images/ug-main-window.png)
1. Type a command in the command box and press Enter to execute it. For example, type **`help`** and press Enter to open the help window.
Some example commands you can try:
* `find n/John` : Shows cyclists whose name contains the complete word `John`.
* `add n/John Doe p/+65 98765432 sos/+65 99999999 e/johnd@example.com f/300 x/Beginner l/any` : Adds a cyclist named `John Doe`, including an emergency contact number supplied using `sos/`.
* `delete +65 98765432` : Requests deletion of the cyclist with this phone number. Enter `yes` to confirm or `no` to cancel.
* `clear` : Deletes all cyclists and all rides.
1. Refer to the [Features](#features) section below for details of each command.

Cyclists are displayed alphabetically by their full name, ignoring letter case, on startup and after `list`, `find` or `ridelist`. Adding a cyclist places them in the correct alphabetical position; editing their name updates their position. Names that are identical ignoring case retain their relative stored order. The visible indexes run consecutively from 1 within the current display, including filtered results. Use phone numbers to target `edit` and `delete` as usual.
* Words in `UPPER_CASE` are the parameters to be supplied by the user.
For example, in `add n/NAME`, replace `NAME` with a value such as `John Doe`.
* Items in square brackets are optional.
For example, `edit PHONE [n/NAME] [f/FTP_LEVEL]` can be used as `edit +65 91234567 n/John Doe` or `edit +65 91234567 f/300`.
* Items followed by `…`​ can appear zero or more times.
For example, `[l/LOCATION]…` in `edit` may be omitted, or written as `l/Punggol` or `l/Punggol l/Marina Bay`.
* Parameters with prefixes can be in any order. Positional arguments must follow the order shown in the command format.
For example, if the command specifies `n/NAME p/PHONE_NUMBER`, `p/PHONE_NUMBER n/NAME` is also acceptable.
* In `rideadd` and `rideedit` only, use `notes/"NOTES"` to keep prefix-looking text inside notes literal.
Ordinary notes need no quotes. See [Ride Add](#adding-a-group-ride-rideadd) for the quoting rules;
this syntax does not apply to other fields or to `ridefind`.
* Extraneous parameters for commands that take no parameters, such as `help`, `list` and `exit`, are ignored.
For example, `help 123` is interpreted as `help`. The exception is [`clear`](#clearing-all-entries-clear), which rejects any extra text because it deletes all your data.

* If you are using a PDF version of this document, be careful when copying and pasting commands that span multiple lines as space characters surrounding line-breaks may be omitted when copied over to the application.
Use these aliases with exactly the same arguments as the full command names. Commands and aliases are case-sensitive.
For example, `re 1 notes/Bring lights` edits ride 1 and `rf all` shows all rides.
The Help menu and Full help window show each alias in parentheses beside its full command name,
for example `rideadd (ra)`. Selecting a Help menu entry inserts the full command name; do not type the parentheses.
Entering an alias while a cyclist deletion confirmation is pending cancels that request,
then processes the alias normally, even if its arguments are invalid.
Cyclique gives you help in two places: the **Help** menu in the menu bar, and the **Full help** window.

Click **Help** in the menu bar to see every command with its format, followed by **Full help...** at the bottom. The commands are listed in this order: `add`, `edit`, `delete`, `find`, `rideadd`, `rideedit`, `ridedelete`, `rideaddcyclist`, `ridedeletecyclist`, `ridelist`, `ridefind`, `list`, `clear`, `help` and `exit`.
Choosing a command from the menu does **not** run it. It places the start of that command in the command box for you to complete, and then you press Enter as usual:
* For most commands, the command word followed by a space is inserted, for example `rideedit `.

* For `add` and `rideadd`, the command word is followed by every required prefix, for example `rideadd n/ from/ to/ l/ d/ f/ s/`. Type a value straight after each prefix. Optional parameters such as `notes/` are not inserted, so type them yourself if you need them.
* `ID` and `PHONE` in `rideaddcyclist ID PHONE` and `ridedeletecyclist ID PHONE` are typed after the command name without a prefix, so no `p/` is inserted.

Choose **Help → Full help...**, press `F1`, or enter `help` to open the Full help window. It lists the usage, parameters and an example for every command. At the bottom it shows a link to the user guide and a **Copy URL** button that copies the link to your clipboard. After you enter `help`, the result box shows `Opened help window.` If the window is already open, Cyclique focuses it instead of opening a second one.
Format: `add n/NAME p/PHONE sos/EMERGENCY_PHONE e/EMAIL f/FTP_LEVEL x/EXPERIENCE_LEVEL l/LOCATION [l/LOCATION]…`

`n/NAME` | The cyclist's name. It may contain Unicode letters (including accented letters), digits and spaces, with combining marks attached to letters or digits. It must start with a letter or digit; blank names and punctuation are rejected. For example, `José Tan` is accepted.

`p/PHONE` | A unique phone number using a `+`, a 1–3 digit country code, one space and at least 3 digits, such as `+65 98765432`. Parentheses, hyphens and blank values are rejected. The number must not belong to another cyclist, including cyclists hidden by a filter.

`sos/EMERGENCY_PHONE` | The cyclist's emergency contact phone number, displayed as **SOS** on their card. Required for new cyclists. It follows the same format as `p/` but may be shared by multiple cyclists and does not determine duplicate cyclists.
`e/EMAIL` | A valid email address, such as `johnd@example.com`. It must be unique across all cyclists, including those hidden by a filter; comparisons ignore letter case.
`f/FTP_LEVEL` | Functional Threshold Power (FTP): a whole number from 1 to 600, in watts.

`l/LOCATION` | A non-blank preferred cycling location containing only letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens or apostrophes. At least one is required. Repeat `l/` for multiple locations, or use `l/any` alone to indicate no location preference. `any` ignores case and cannot be combined with another location.
All fields are required. Only `l/` may be repeated; repeating any other prefix is rejected.
Prefixes can be entered in any order. Cyclists may share a name or emergency contact number,
but their own phone numbers and email addresses must be unique.
On success, the result box shows `New person added:` followed by the cyclist's details, including
`Emergency phone:`. The new card shows the number as **SOS**. Cyclique restores the full cyclist
list, places the new card in alphabetical order and saves the data automatically.
Examples (use phone numbers and email addresses that are not already stored):
* `add n/John Doe p/+65 98765432 sos/+65 99999999 e/johnd@example.com f/300 x/Beginner l/any` adds John with an FTP of 300 W, Beginner experience and no location preference.

* `add n/Betsy Crowe sos/+65 99999999 e/betsycrowe@example.com p/+65 91234567 f/250 x/Advanced l/Punggol l/Seletar` adds Betsy with two preferred locations. Sharing John's emergency contact number is allowed.
![Add success showing John Doe's SOS number and cycling profile alongside the existing cyclists and rides](images/ug-add-success.png)
*After the first example, John appears after Chloe in the alphabetical list. The two existing rides are unchanged.*
Missing required fields, blank values, invalid values and repeated single-valued prefixes are rejected.
A phone or email conflict reports `Another cyclist already has this phone number or email.`
These rejected commands leave existing records unchanged and do not add a cyclist.
Shows every cyclist currently stored in the address book.
* Removes any active `find` or [`ridelist`](#listing-cyclists-registered-for-a-ride-ridelist) filter and restores all cyclists. The result box shows `Listed all persons.`
* Affects only the cyclist panel. It does not change the Rides panel; use `ridefind all` to show every ride again.
* Displays cyclist cards alphabetically by full name, ignoring case. Names that are identical ignoring case retain their stored order.
* Each card shows the cyclist's name, phone number, SOS number, email, FTP, experience level and preferred locations. A missing SOS number is shown as **Not provided**.
* If there are no cyclists, the cyclist panel is empty and the result still shows `Listed all persons.`
Updates an existing cyclist's contact details or cycling profile.

* The unprefixed `PHONE` identifies the cyclist to edit. It must match exactly one cyclist in the **displayed list**. Use `list` first if a filter hides the cyclist. Card indexes cannot be used as the target.

* Include `+`, the country code and one space in the target phone number, for example `+65 91234567`. A malformed target reports the specific phone-validation error; omitting the target reports the command usage.
* `p/PHONE`, if supplied, is the cyclist's **replacement** phone number. For example, `edit +65 98765432 p/+65 91111111` targets the old number and replaces it with the new number.
* Supply at least one optional field. Otherwise, Cyclique reports `At least one field to edit must be provided.`

* Supplied fields follow the [Add field rules](#adding-a-cyclist-add). Only `l/` may be repeated. Phone numbers and email addresses must remain unique across all cyclists, including hidden records; email comparisons ignore case. Keeping the cyclist's own current phone or email is allowed.

* Omitted fields remain unchanged. Supplying one or more `l/` fields replaces the **entire** preferred location set; it does not append locations. Blank `l/` is invalid. Use `l/any` alone for no location preference.
* Omitting `sos/` preserves the existing emergency contact number. Blank `sos/` is invalid and cannot remove the number.

* An edited FTP must meet the minimum power of every ride the cyclist is registered for, including rides hidden by a filter. Equality with the minimum is allowed. If it is too low, the entire edit is rejected with the conflicting ride's ID, name and minimum FTP; accompanying field changes are not applied. Remove the cyclist from the affected rides first if they should no longer participate, or edit the ride requirements before lowering their FTP.
On success, the result box shows `Edited person:` followed by the updated details and saves the changes.
Any active `find` or `ridelist` filter remains applied. A cyclist who no longer matches the search disappears
from the displayed results; use `list` to show all cyclists again. Matching cyclists remain in alphabetical
order, so a name edit may move a card to a different position. Changing the cyclist's own phone number also
updates that number in every ride roster they belong to, preserving their memberships and visibility in

* `edit +65 98765432 sos/+65 98888888` updates only the emergency number; all other fields remain unchanged. This can also be used independently of the previous example.

### Locating persons by name, phone or emergency number: `find`
Finds persons by name keywords, phone numbers, emergency contact numbers, FTP, experience level and preferred location.

`n/NAME_KEYWORD` | A single name word or multiple complete name words. Matching is case-insensitive and each supplied word must appear as a complete word in the same order; `n/hans` matches `Hans` but `n/Han` does not. A multi-word value such as `n/John Doe` matches names containing `John` followed by `Doe`, even when other words appear between them.
`p/PHONE` | A complete phone number using a `+`, a 1–3 digit country code, one space and at least 3 digits. Matching is exact; `p/+65 963` does not match `+65 96320842`.

`sos/EMERGENCY_PHONE` | A complete emergency contact number using the same validation and exact matching as `p/`. Only cyclists with an emergency number matching the supplied value are shown. Cyclists whose emergency number is missing or different are not shown.
`f/MIN_FTP` | A whole number from 1 to 600, inclusive. Matches cyclists whose FTP is greater than or equal to the supplied value in watts; both `f/1` and `f/600` are valid.
`x/EXPERIENCE` | `Beginner`, `Intermediate` or `Advanced`, ignoring case. Repeat `x/` to match any of the supplied experience levels.

`l/LOCATION` | A preferred location, ignoring case. Complete words within the supplied location are matched in order, so `l/Coast` and `l/East Coast` match `East Coast Park` but `l/Coas` does not. Repeat `l/` to match any supplied location. A cyclist with `l/any` matches every location criterion.
At least one criterion is required. Each prefix may be repeated except `f/`, which accepts only one value. Values
within the same field use `OR`, while different fields use `AND`; for example, `find n/Hans n/Bo f/250` matches
cyclists named `Hans` or `Bo` whose FTP is at least 250 W. Prefix order does not matter. Text after a prefix belongs
to that field until the next recognised prefix, so full names and locations containing spaces can be entered normally.
The command filters only the displayed cyclist list and does not change saved records. Matching cyclists remain in
alphabetical order, ignoring case. The result message reports how many cyclists match; an empty result is valid and
leaves the cyclist panel empty. Use `list` to remove the current filter and display all cyclists again.
Invalid phone numbers, FTP values, experience levels, preferred locations, name values and duplicate `f/` prefixes
are rejected without changing the current displayed list. A name or phone criterion searches only the corresponding
field; emergency contact numbers are not treated as the cyclist's own phone number.
* `find n/John Doe` returns cyclists whose names contain `John` followed by `Doe`, ignoring case,
even if there are other words in between.
* `find n/alex p/+65 96320842` returns only people whose name contains `alex` and whose phone number is `+65 96320842`.
* `find l/Punggol x/Intermediate f/250` returns cyclists whose preferred location is Punggol, experience level is Intermediate,
and FTP is at least 250 W.
* `find l/East Coast` returns cyclists whose preferred location contains `East Coast`, such as `East Coast Park`.
* `find sos/+65 99999999` returns cyclists with that emergency contact number.
* `find x/Beginner x/Intermediate` returns cyclists with either experience level.
* `find` with no criteria is rejected with the command usage instructions.
* `find f/0` is rejected because FTP must be a whole number from 1 to 600.
* A phone number, FTP value, experience level or location that does not follow the constraints above is rejected
Deletes a cyclist only after you check their details and confirm in the command box.
Format: `delete PHONE`, then enter a separate confirmation or cancellation reply.

* Use the cyclist's own complete phone number, including country code and exactly one space, for example `+65 98765432`. The country code contains 1–3 digits; the number after the space contains at least 3 digits. Do not use a card index or the `p/` prefix.
* A malformed target reports the specific phone-validation error; omitting the target reports the command usage.

* The number must identify exactly one cyclist in the **displayed list**. A cyclist hidden by a filter cannot be deleted; use `list` to show all cyclists first. Multiple displayed matches are rejected.

* The result panel shows `Delete this cyclist?` followed by the target's details, including their emergency number, and warns `This also removes them from all ride rosters.` No cyclist, roster or saved data changes at this stage.
* Enter `y` or `yes` to confirm, or `n` or `no` to cancel. Replies ignore letter case and surrounding spaces, so `YeS` and ` NO ` are accepted.
* Cancellation shows `Deletion cancelled.` and preserves cyclist records, ride rosters, the current filter and saved data.
* An invalid reply, such as `maybe`, `yes please` or an unknown command, reports `Invalid confirmation.` and keeps waiting for a valid reply. It does not cancel the request or change data.

* A recognised command cancels the pending deletion and then runs. The result shows `Deletion cancelled.` followed by that command's usual output or error, even if its arguments are invalid. Another valid `delete PHONE` starts a fresh request. Command names remain case-sensitive: `list` cancels, but `LIST` is an invalid reply.
* Closing or restarting Cyclique discards any pending request. Without a pending request, `yes` and `no` report `Unknown command.`
Confirmation shows `Deleted person:` followed by the deleted cyclist's details. Their card disappears,
and their phone number is removed from **all ride rosters**. The rides themselves, other cyclists and
their memberships remain. The change is saved automatically. There is no undo command.

Adds a group ride that an organiser plans to lead.
Format: `rideadd n/NAME from/FROM to/TO l/LOCATION d/DISTANCE f/MIN_POWER s/MAX_GROUP_SIZE [notes/NOTES]`

`n/NAME` | The name of the ride. Unicode letters (including accented letters), digits and spaces, with combining marks attached to letters or digits. It must start with a letter or digit; blank names and punctuation are rejected.

`from/FROM` | When the ride starts, written as `DD-MM-YYYY TTTT` (day-month-year, followed by exactly one space and the time). `TTTT` uses the 24-hour clock from `0000` to `2359`, for example `25-10-2026 0630`. Both the date and time are required. The date must be a real calendar date, including the correct leap-year rules.
`to/TO` | When the ride ends, in the same format as `from/`. It must not be earlier than `from/` (the same time is allowed).
`l/LOCATION` | One non-blank location. English letters (`A–Z`, `a–z`), digits (`0–9`), spaces, hyphens and apostrophes only.
`d/DISTANCE` | The distance in kilometres, from `0.01` to `999999.99`. Use 1–6 digits before the decimal point and, optionally, 1–2 digits after it, such as `45` or `45.5`.
`f/MIN_POWER` | The minimum power a cyclist needs to join, in watts. Use 1–3 digits representing a whole number from 1 to 600, the same range as a cyclist's FTP.
`s/MAX_GROUP_SIZE` | The most cyclists that can join. Use 1–9 digits representing a whole number from 1 to 999999999.

`notes/NOTES` | Optional. If supplied, it must contain 1–10 words separated by whitespace, including Unicode spaces such as non-breaking, EM, narrow non-breaking and ideographic spaces. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed; repeated whitespace is stored as single ordinary spaces. Omit the prefix for no notes; empty or whitespace-only `notes/` is rejected when adding a ride. These rules also apply inside quoted notes.

Every field except `notes/` is required and must have a value. Each prefix can be used only once, in any order. Put whitespace before each prefix; spaces around values are trimmed. Command words and prefixes are case-sensitive: use `rideadd` and `from/`, for example. Names, locations and notes retain the capitalisation you enter. Enter numeric values without units, signs, commas or scientific notation; zero and negative values are rejected. Leading zeroes count towards the digit limits and are removed from stored numeric values.
Ordinary notes such as `notes/Bring water` do not need quotation marks. To include recognised ride prefixes
(`n/`, `from/`, `to/`, `l/`, `d/`, `f/`, `s/` or `notes/`) literally, put a double quote immediately after
`notes/` and another at the end of the notes: `notes/"Bring camera with aperture f/2"`.
The surrounding quotes are not stored, and recognised prefixes inside them do not create or change other fields.
Other parameters may appear before or after quoted notes. Unicode whitespace is allowed after the closing quote,
including at the end of the command. For a following parameter, use an ordinary space immediately before its
prefix; non-breaking and narrow non-breaking spaces alone do not introduce a parameter.
The same 1–10-word limit and whitespace rules apply.
The first double quote after the opening quote closes the value. Missing closing quotes, empty or whitespace-only
quoted notes, and extra text after the closing quote before the next recognised parameter are rejected.
For example, `notes/"Bring water"extra` and `notes/"Bring water" q/test` are invalid.
In unquoted notes, double quotes away from the beginning are literal, as in `notes/Bring a "camera"`.
A double quote immediately after `notes/` always starts quoted-notes syntax; it is not stored as a literal quote.
Quoted notes cannot contain literal double quotes, and escaping is unsupported: backslashes are literal and do
not escape quotes. These quoting rules apply only to `rideadd` and `rideedit`, including their aliases.

Rides may be in the past, cross midnight or span multiple days. The end must be on or after the start: for an overnight ride, enter the later date in `to/` as well as the time. Equal start and end date/times are allowed.

Each new ride gets a persistent ID automatically. A new empty book starts at 1; an existing book continues from its saved counter. IDs increase in creation order and are never reused, including after deletion, `clear` or restarting. Check the assigned ID in the result or ride card; it is not the card's list position. A new ride has no cyclists on its roster yet. Even rides with identical details are allowed, because their IDs differ.

On success, the result box shows `New ride added:` followed by the assigned ID and complete ride details, and the change is saved automatically. The right-hand **Rides** panel updates immediately, with the new ride after existing rides. An active `ridefind` filter is retained and may hide the new card; use `ridefind all` to show every ride. Cyclist records and the current cyclist filter are unchanged. Each ride card shows its ID and name, period, location, distance, minimum power, maximum group size and roster, plus a **Notes** line if notes are present.
* `rideadd n/Sunday Sunrise Ride from/25-10-2026 0630 to/25-10-2026 0930 l/East Coast Park d/45 f/180 s/3 notes/Bring lights and a spare tube`
* `rideadd n/Evening Spin from/27-10-2026 1800 to/27-10-2026 1930 l/Punggol d/30.5 f/150 s/8`
* `rideadd n/Camera Ride from/29-10-2026 1600 to/29-10-2026 1800 l/East Coast d/20 f/180 s/2 notes/"Bring camera with aperture f/2"`

The first example adds a 45 km ride with minimum power 180 W and room for three cyclists. The second adds a ride without notes; its feedback includes `Notes: None`. If the sample rides already exist, these commands add separate rides with new IDs.
The Camera Ride example stores `Bring camera with aperture f/2` as its notes, without the quotes,
